page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance within the High Clock Speed instance family. Built on KVM architecture with dedicated CPU scheduling, it features a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor providing 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI support. System memory totals 32 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

The server does not include local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for persistent data operations. Networking capability provides a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps. The instance contains no dedicated GPU acceleration hardware, relying solely on CPU compute capability for execution. Hardware-level cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES instructions alongside bit manipulation extensions such as BMI2 and ADX.

Benchmark results place the instance in the median tier across general computing categories. In stress-ng, single-core testing reached 1435.0 while multi-core throughput registered at 15316.01. Memory read bandwidth measured 87.94 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks, accompanied by write speeds of 37.05 GB/sec. Application tests showed 15.25 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 12.43 GB/sec in static web serving. Text and language model processing remained effective on smaller 135M parameter models at 935.61 prompt tokens per second, but throughput declined to weak percentiles on 7B models at 23.1 prompt tokens per second.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance and absence of local disks, cost efficiency is centered on raw processing density rather than large in-memory footprints or high-throughput storage caches. The instance is positioned for CPU-bound computational tasks, continuous integration and software compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, and stateless backend services.
